findings.text: non-blocking: `_PARSED_INDEX_DOCUMENTS` re-implements the capability `reckon/file_memo.py:358` `memoized` already owns (memoise a per-file parse against the file's stat identity), which this module already imports at review_records.py:34; kind, path and variant=code-stamp plus a read_only_region would serve the same need, so the addition duplicates the owner instead of extending it.

non-blocking: a cache hit hands every caller the same mutable dict, so the safety of the process-wide copy rests only on the convention at review_records.py:2017-2018 that writers use `_fresh_index_document`; `file_memo.memoized` enforces this by handing out a copy or a read-only view, which this path forgoes.

item_verdicts.diff: read all four commits against base 869274dbfa; they add the parse cache, route writers and the settle path through a private parse, drop the cache on persist and re-check a held mapping against the code stamp, changing three files only.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when names tests/test_an_unchanged_index_is_parsed_once.py asserting 100 calls parse once and the first call after record_written parses once more and returns the new entry, with a base negative control that fails; the test at tests/test_an_unchanged_index_is_parsed_once.py:93 and :103 is exactly that, and logs/negative-control.log:25 reproduces "100 reads of an unchanged index document parsed it 100 times".
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is to parse an unchanged review index document once per process; reckon/crew/review_records.py:2031-2056 keys the kept mapping on the file's inode, size and mtime and returns it on a key match, exactly as the goal states.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, four commits, pop arms 192 passed and 193 passed with 0 failure ids reported and on disk, negative control 1 failed / EXIT=1, and every log it cites opens with revision and literal command and ends in a bare EXIT=.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the source prompt's fence is reckon/crew/review_records.py, the node test, and the fragment/figures; `git diff --name-only 869274dbfa..47fa615554` names review_records.py, tests/test_an_unchanged_index_is_parsed_once.py and the fragment, and no figure was written.

justifications.durability: tests/test_an_unchanged_index_is_parsed_once.py:93 fails with 100 parses if the cache is removed, but the code-stamp re-check at review_records.py:2053 is covered only by the pre-existing tests/test_the_review_store_index_re_reads_only_what_changed.py, not by a new assertion.
justifications.evidence: logs/after-arm.log records 52 passed EXIT=0 at 47fa6155 and logs/negative-control.log:25 shows the defect was reproduced at base; the fragment's ruff claim is unlogged, though I re-ran ruff on both staged files and it is clean.
justifications.fit: the added _PARSED_INDEX_DOCUMENTS at reckon/crew/review_records.py:2004 follows the module's existing store-keyed mapping shape (_DOCUMENT_MAPS, _STORE_INDEXES) and no name violates the naming rules.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/review_records.py:2047-2053 returns the kept mapping when (st_ino, st_size, st_mtime_ns) matches and parses afresh otherwise, which is the goal's mechanism and its measure.
justifications.reuse: reckon/file_memo.py:358 `memoized` already owns stat-keyed per-file parse memoisation, is imported at review_records.py:34, and the added cache duplicates it rather than extending it.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in git diff 869274dbfa..47fa615554 lies inside the declared write paths, and the fragment is the only prose added.
